session_covered: US and European sessions of Monday 26 October
intro: Covers the US and European sessions of Monday 26 October. This brief was delayed from the early-morning slot because the US session had not yet closed; SPI futures direction is a near-flat call across sources (see footnotes).
footnotes: Brent, gold and the 10-year yield differ slightly between sources (Brent US$115.60/-1.0%, gold US$4,026.20/+0.5%, 10-year 4.98%); the FNArena table values are shown, and the differences are timing/rounding. Commodity prices are CFD-based reference prices.

setup.summary: SPI 200 futures are at about 8,821 (December contract), essentially flat versus the prior day-session close (roughly -0.07% to +0.07% depending on source), which implies a broadly unchanged ASX 200 open near 8,810, a change of about 0 points. Futures had already risen during Monday's day session, so the Wall Street gain looks largely priced in. The ASX 200 closed Monday at 8,809.9, up 14.7 points (+0.17%), recovering from early losses; Materials, Real Estate and Technology each gained more than 1% while Consumer Staples fell 1.54%.

local_events: No major scheduled Australian data releases; several AGMs are due (including CSL and PLS Group). Q3 CPI is due tomorrow (Wednesday).
what_moved: US equities rose, led by technology and chip stocks, after Anthropic filed for a Nasdaq IPO, reviving the AI trade ahead of a heavy week of megacap earnings and the Fed decision. Oil eased about 1% on diplomatic efforts to de-escalate Middle East tensions, and the VIX fell to 18.39. Technology and consumer discretionary outperformed; full S&P 500 sector percentages were not available. In Europe the FTSE 100 gained 0.7% and the DAX 0.9%.

news.headline: Anthropic files for Nasdaq IPO
news.summary: The AI developer filed to list under the ticker ANT, reportedly targeting up to US$100bn at a valuation near US$2 trillion, which would be the largest listing on record; the filing showed H1 revenue of US$16.3bn alongside large losses.

news.headline: Fed decision Wednesday, pause expected
news.summary: The Fed meets this week with a hold widely expected, though traders still see a December hike as possible; PCE inflation and Q3 GDP follow on Thursday.

news.headline: Meta plans up to US$95bn equity raise
news.summary: The AI-infrastructure funding plan pushed Meta shares down about 1.8% and fuelled debate over whether heavy AI spending is paying off, with about a third of the S&P 500 reporting this week.

news.headline: Oil eases on de-escalation diplomacy
news.summary: Brent fell about 1% to US$115.33/bbl after Saudi and Iranian officials met in Tehran, though Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia continue and crude remains near six-month highs.

news.headline: Brazil election shock hits local assets
news.summary: Lula's fourth-term win against market expectations triggered Brazil's worst equity day since March 2020 and the real's worst day against the US dollar since at least 1994.

news.headline: US midterms on 3 November
news.summary: RBC sees a split Congress as neutral to modestly positive for US equities and a Democratic sweep, which betting markets favour, as neutral to negative.

news.headline: Australian Q3 CPI due tomorrow
news.summary: The inflation print lands the same day as the Fed decision, with the Australian dollar softer at US$0.7018 and the US dollar index up 0.2% to 102.00.

coming_up: Wednesday 28 October: Australian September-quarter CPI, and the US Fed rate decision (early Thursday morning Sydney time). Thursday 29 October (US): PCE inflation and Q3 GDP. US midterm elections: Tuesday 3 November.
